title: The Scientific Endeavour: Investigations and Lab Safety
seo_title: Secondary 1 Science: Scientific Method and Lab Safety Worksheets with Answers
standard_text: Understand how science works: ask questions, form hypotheses and plan fair investigations with independent, dependent and controlled variables; collect, present and analyse data and draw conclusions; use laboratory apparatus and SI units correctly and safely; recognise hazard symbols; appreciate that scientific knowledge changes with new evidence (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 science worksheets for Singapore students on the scientific endeavour: variables and fair tests, results and graphs, apparatus, SI units, hazard symbols and lab safety. With answers.
key_big: Change one variable, measure one, keep the rest the same.
key_sub: Repeat, average and look for anomalous results.
body_html:
How to think about it

Science answers questions by testing ideas with fair experiments.

  • Independent variable: what you change. Dependent variable: what you measure. Controlled variables: kept the same.
  • Repeat measurements and take an average. Look out for anomalous results.
  • Use the right apparatus and SI units: metre, kilogram, second, kelvin.
  • Follow safety rules: goggles, tie back hair, read hazard symbols, use the blue flame for heating.
Example

Testing how temperature affects the time for sugar to dissolve. Dependent variable?

It is what you measure

Answer: the time for the sugar to dissolve

Example

Which apparatus measures 25.0 cm³ of liquid accurately for a titration?

A beaker is only rough

Answer: a pipette

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the independent (changed) and dependent (measured) variables.
  • Thinking a hypothesis is the result. It is a testable idea.
  • Measuring volume with a beaker. Use a measuring cylinder, pipette or burette.
  • Heating with the yellow luminous flame. Use the blue flame.

faq.q: What is the difference between independent and dependent variables?
faq.a: The independent variable is the one you change. The dependent variable is the one you measure.
To check that results are reliable and to find anomalous results. We then take an average.

faq.q: Which Bunsen burner flame is used for heating?
faq.a: The blue non-luminous flame, with the air hole open.

items.q: Which equipment measures time accurately?
items.e: Time in seconds.

items.q: Imran is investigating how the height of a ramp affects the distance a toy car travels. What is the variable that should be kept constant?
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Jun Jie is investigating how the temperature of water affects the time for sugar to dissolve. What is the variable that should be kept constant?
c: the time for the sugar to dissolve
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: What is a prediction?
c: what you think will happen, with a reason
items.e: Made before the test.

items.q: Xin Yi is investigating how the surface area of a container affects the rate of evaporation. What is the independent variable (the one that is changed)?
c: the surface area of the container
the volume of water lost in a day
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Farah is investigating how the type of surface affects the force needed to pull a block. What is the variable that should be kept constant?
c: the force needed to pull the block
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Siti is investigating how the thickness of a cloth affects the time for hot water to cool. What is the independent variable (the one that is changed)?
c: the starting temperature of the water
the temperature of the water after 10 minutes

items.q: Which equipment measures force?
items.e: Force is measured in newtons.

items.q: Arjun is investigating how the concentration of acid affects the time for a magnesium ribbon to react. What is the variable that should be kept constant?
c: the length of the magnesium ribbon
the time for the magnesium to disappear
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Why should only one variable be changed in a fair test?
c: so the results are always the same
so that any change in the results is caused by that variable only
items.e: All other variables are kept constant.

items.q: What is a hypothesis?
c: a possible explanation that can be tested by an experiment
a fact that can never change
items.e: For example: 'Sugar dissolves faster in hot water because particles move faster.'

items.q: What is a conclusion?
c: what the results show, answering the question
items.e: Based on evidence.

items.q: What is an anomalous result?
c: a result that does not fit the pattern of the others
items.e: Check it or repeat it.

items.q: Aisha is investigating how the temperature of water affects the time for sugar to dissolve. What is the dependent variable (the one that is measured)?
c: the time for the sugar to dissolve
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Wei Jie is investigating how the thickness of a cloth affects the time for hot water to cool. What is the variable that should be kept constant?
c: the temperature of the water after 10 minutes
the starting temperature of the water
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: Hui Min is investigating how the height of a ramp affects the distance a toy car travels. What is the dependent variable (the one that is measured)?
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: What should you do with an anomalous result?
c: repeat the test or leave it out of the mean
items.e: It may be a mistake.

items.q: Wei Ling is investigating how the length of a pendulum affects the time for one swing. What is the dependent variable (the one that is measured)?
items.e: Independent: changed. Dependent: measured. Controlled: kept the same so the test is fair.

items.q: What is a fair test?
c: a test where only one variable is changed and the others are kept the same
items.e: Change one thing.

items.q: Why do scientists repeat measurements?
c: to check results and make them more reliable
because the first result is always wrong
items.e: Repeats show if results agree.

items.q: How should you read the volume of water in a measuring cylinder?

items.q: What is the SI unit of temperature?
items.e: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin (K).

items.q: What is the SI unit of time?

items.q: What is the SI unit of force?

items.q: What is the SI unit of mass?

items.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
items.e: The SI unit of electric current is the ampere (A).

To measure the volume of a liquid.
To hold and heat liquids (it gives only a rough volume).
To evaporate a solution to get the solid.
items.e: An evaporating dish is used to evaporate a solution to get the solid.

items.q: What is a beaker used for?
c: To measure the volume of a liquid.
To support a beaker over a Bunsen burner.
To hold and heat liquids (it gives only a rough volume).
items.e: A beaker is used to hold and heat liquids (it gives only a rough volume).

items.q: What is the SI unit of length?
items.e: The SI unit of length is the metre (m).

items.q: What is a pipette used for?
c: To transfer a fixed volume of liquid accurately.
To add a liquid drop by drop and measure the volume added accurately.
To evaporate a solution to get the solid.
To hold apparatus firmly in place.
items.e: A pipette is used to transfer a fixed volume of liquid accurately.

items.q: What is a retort stand with a clamp used for?
c: To add a liquid drop by drop and measure the volume added accurately.
To hold apparatus firmly in place.
To hold a hot test tube.
items.e: A retort stand with a clamp is used to hold apparatus firmly in place.

items.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
items.e: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J).

items.q: What does the hazard symbol for a explosive substance warn you about?
c: The substance destroys living tissue and some materials on contact.
The substance can cause redness or blisters on the skin, or is less dangerous than toxic.
The substance may explode when heated, struck or exposed to a flame.
items.e: This is the meaning of the explosive symbol.

items.q: Which Bunsen burner flame is used for heating?
c: the yellow luminous flame, with the air hole closed
the blue non-luminous flame, with the air hole open
a flame with the gas turned off
items.e: The blue flame is hotter and does not leave soot.

items.q: Which hazard label is most suitable for dilute ammonia solution?
items.e: Dilute ammonia solution can cause redness or blisters on the skin, or is less dangerous than toxic.

items.q: What is a stopwatch used for?
c: To support a beaker over a Bunsen burner.
To transfer a fixed volume of liquid accurately.
items.e: A stopwatch is used to measure time.

items.q: Why must you wear safety goggles when heating chemicals?
c: to see the flame more clearly
to protect your eyes from splashes and hot chemicals
items.e: Goggles protect against splashes.

items.q: What does the hazard symbol for a harmful or irritant substance warn you about?
c: The substance destroys living tissue and some materials on contact.
The substance can cause redness or blisters on the skin, or is less dangerous than toxic.
The substance provides oxygen and makes other substances burn more fiercely.
items.e: This is the meaning of the harmful or irritant symbol.

items.q: Why should the air hole of a Bunsen burner be closed when it is lit?
c: to get a visible yellow safety flame
items.e: The safety flame is easy to see when the burner is not in use.

items.q: What is a thermometer used for?
c: To transfer a fixed volume of liquid accurately.
To hold apparatus firmly in place.
To add a liquid drop by drop and measure the volume added accurately.
items.e: A thermometer is used to measure temperature.

items.q: Which hazard label is most suitable for mercury?
items.e: Mercury can cause death or serious harm if swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin.

items.q: Which hazard label is most suitable for a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen?
items.e: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen may explode when heated, struck or exposed to a flame.

items.q: What is the SI unit of volume?
items.e: The SI unit of volume is the cubic metre (m³).

items.q: Which apparatus is used to measure mass?
items.e: An electronic balance is used to measure mass.

items.q: Scientific knowledge sometimes changes. Why?
c: New evidence may show that an old idea needs to be improved.
items.e: This is how science progresses.

items.q: Which apparatus is used to hold apparatus firmly in place?
c: a retort stand with a clamp
items.e: A retort stand with a clamp is used to hold apparatus firmly in place.

items.q: What does the hazard symbol for a toxic substance warn you about?
c: The substance provides oxygen and makes other substances burn more fiercely.
The substance may explode when heated, struck or exposed to a flame.
The substance can cause death or serious harm if swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin.
items.e: This is the meaning of the toxic symbol.

items.q: When heating a liquid in a test tube, where should you point the mouth of the tube?
c: away from yourself and other people
items.e: Hot liquid may spurt out.

items.q: What is a measuring cylinder used for?
c: To hold liquids that are swirled, so they do not splash out.
To measure the volume of a liquid.
items.e: A measuring cylinder is used to measure the volume of a liquid.

items.q: What does the hazard symbol for a flammable substance warn you about?
c: The substance can cause redness or blisters on the skin, or is less dangerous than toxic.
The substance provides oxygen and makes other substances burn more fiercely.
The substance can cause death or serious harm if swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin.
items.e: This is the meaning of the flammable symbol.

items.q: What does the hazard symbol for a oxidising substance warn you about?
c: The substance destroys living tissue and some materials on contact.
The substance can cause death or serious harm if swallowed, breathed in or absorbed through the skin.
The substance provides oxygen and makes other substances burn more fiercely.
items.e: This is the meaning of the oxidising symbol.

items.q: Which apparatus is used to hold and heat liquids (it gives only a rough volume)?
c: a tripod stand and wire gauze
items.e: A beaker is used to hold and heat liquids (it gives only a rough volume).

items.q: A student repeats an experiment three times: 24 s, 25 s, 41 s. What should she do?
c: treat 41 s as anomalous, repeat it, and average the reliable results
items.e: Anomalous results do not fit the pattern.
